name: Browsers and Search Engines
description: The programs we browse with and the sites we search with, from Mosaic and AltaVista to Chrome and Google.

checkpoints.name: The first web
checkpoints.note: Tim Berners-Lee builds the web at CERN, and in 1993 the Mosaic browser puts pictures and text on one page. Netscape follows a year later, and the first directories and search engines appear to help people find their way.

checkpoints.name: The first browser war
checkpoints.note: Internet Explorer arrives in August 1995 and, bundled with Windows, overtakes Netscape. By the time Internet Explorer 6 ships in 2001 the war is over.

checkpoints.name: The second browser war
checkpoints.note: Firefox 1.0 (2004) and then Chrome (2008) win users back from a stalled Internet Explorer, until Microsoft replaces it with Edge in Windows 10 in 2015.

checkpoints.name: Chrome on top
checkpoints.note: Chrome is the most used browser by a wide margin, and most of its rivals are built on the same engine. Internet Explorer is retired in 2022, and search begins to share the screen with AI assistants.
